title: At the market
description: Name the people and the things at a market stall.
grammar: gender and articles, and the plural of nouns
grammarNote: Some market words end in -o and some in -a, and the ending tells you which.

explanation.summary: A market is people and objects. The nouns are ordinary ones, but they are the words a learner hears first when they go shopping for food.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El vendedor, el cliente, el carrito, el toldo, el almacén and el ticket are masculine. La bandeja, la báscula, la etiqueta and la fila are feminine. A folder is la carpeta, and the scale that weighs your shopping is la báscula.

sections.heading: Words that change in the plural
sections.body: The plural adds -s or -es: el vendedor becomes los vendedores and la etiqueta becomes las etiquetas. Two words lose the accent in the plural: el almacén becomes los almacenes and la etiqueta becomes las etiquetas.

examples.es: hay mucha gente en la fila
examples.en: there are a lot of people in the queue

items.note: Masculine: el vendedor. The feminine is la vendedora.
Masculine: el carrito. It is the small -ito that makes it small.
Feminine: la báscula. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el almacén. The accent marks the stress.
Masculine: el ticket. In Spain it is also el tique.

drills.meaning: the label is on the box
the customers are in the warehouse
drills.note: A noun ending in a vowel adds -es.

drills.meaning: I put the items on the tray
drills.note: Bandeja is feminine, so la bandeja.
